//: Who may touch what, written down BEFORE anyone starts. Two parcels claiming one file is the failure this file exists to prevent, and it costs one second to catch here instead of four hours in a merge. Read docs/parallel-dev.md first — it carries the brief to paste and the rule about not committing while agents are still typing.
//seams: Files everything needs. A parcel may ADD up to three lines to one of these and delete none, and must declare which lines up front. Two one-line additions merge by keeping both; two thirty-line edits merge into something nobody can verify. TWO STATED EXCEPTIONS, because the three-line grammar would make them unusable: scripts/build-kb.ts admits one appended Corpus const plus this door's name on the CORPORA line, and shared/roster.ts admits one whole appended agent entry. Both are appends at the end of a list, which is the shape that merges.
//frozen: Nobody edits these during a parallel run. A change here invalidates every parcel at once.
//alone: Parcels marked runAlone touch the room, the panel or the shell — everything reads those, and two agents in them at once produce a merge nobody can check. One agent, let it finish, then start the others.
//order: Three at a time, and NEVER two doors in the same wave — every door appends a Corpus const to scripts/build-kb.ts and a name to its CORPORA line, and they share one working tree. Wave 1: spend-limits, door-linkedin-ads, favicon-and-social. Wave 2: door-linkedin-automation, llms-txt, legal-name-display. Wave 3: door-ai-builds, payment-link. Then the runAlone ones, one after another. And do not let two agents run `npm run verify` at the same moment: vite empties dist/ on every build, so a concurrent build reads a directory another one is deleting. Ask them to report and run it yourself, or stagger it.

spend-limits.why: An agent reply costs about a quarter of a cent and a human conversation about three. Two agents answering each other cost about $4 an hour on this model — which is not frightening, and that is the danger: left running it is $104 a day and nobody notices, because nothing alarming happens at $4.
spend-limits.done: READ docs/OPENAI-SDK-NOTES.md first: the token-accounting recipe is already written there, so do not re-derive it. Today AgentStreamChunk carries only delta, citations and error, and create() sets no stream_options — so no token count, dollar figure or model name reaches the caller at all, and a cost log written today would be invented. The seam above is what makes the numbers exist. Then three independent bounds, because each fails differently: a count of turns per room, a clock that stops an agent after N minutes of activity, and a budget in money per room per month, warned at 80% and paused at 100%. One cost event per turn — room, agent, model, tokens in, tokens out, dollars — and nothing more. The count is taken atomically BEFORE the model call, so two messages arriving together cannot both pass. ON THE AGENT-REPLIES-TO-AGENT INVARIANT: check before you test it. POST /api/workspaces/:token/messages hard-codes authorKind "visitor" and resolveAgent takes no author argument, so a server-authored message cannot currently reach the reply path at all — the invariant holds by construction rather than by a rule. Say which it is in your report, and write the test against what the code actually does.

outside-agent.done: Somebody else's agent is admitted to ONE thread, watch-only by default, with a call budget, an expiry and a visible revoke.
